Groq LPU.description: Groq Language Processing Unit (LPU) is an ASIC architecture using synchronous dataflow execution with on-chip SRAM. Multiple LPU chips are connected via a high-speed interconnect. Unlike GPUs, Groq has no external memory — all model weights and activations reside in on-chip SRAM, eliminating the memory wall.

independent_sources.finding: Official platform page confirms 1,000 tok/s/user guarantee — this is a per-user SLA, not peak benchmark. More conservative than vendor peak claims.
Third-party analysis confirms Groq's deterministic latency advantage. Architecture verified as ASIC with on-chip SRAM.
Independent benchmark confirms Groq outperforms GPUs in single-stream latency. Multi-stream aggregate throughput not verified.

limitations: ASIC — fixed architecture, can't run arbitrary models without recompilation
Single-stream optimized; multi-stream aggregate throughput unverified
Model support limited to popular architectures (Llama, Mistral, etc.)

Cerebras WSE-3.description: Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine 3 uses an entire 804mm² silicon wafer as a single processor with 922,368 AI cores and 21 GB of on-chip SRAM. No chip interconnect latency — the entire wafer acts as one massive processor with 160 TB/s on-chip bandwidth.

claims.claim: Up to 750 tok/s for GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast

independent_sources.finding: Official page shows 750 tok/s for GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast — LOWER than stage 02 claims of 1,800-3,000 tok/s. Stage 02 numbers may have used peak benchmarks from different model sizes or earlier WSE-2 generation.
Cerebras confirmed as wafer-scale architecture with 21 PB/s on-chip SRAM bandwidth. Architecture verified.

limitations: Stage 02 benchmark numbers (1,800-3,000 tok/s) appear inflated vs official 750 tok/s
Extremely expensive — not available for purchase, only via cloud API
Limited to models that fit on-chip SRAM (21 GB effective)
Pricing: ~$1-3M per wafer + cloud usage fees

SambaNova DataScale SN3000.description: SambaNova DataScale uses custom RDU (Rainbow Dataflow Unit) ASICs with on-chip SRAM. Sold as complete DataScale systems (not individual chips). Architecture eliminates memory wall via dataflow execution with SRAM at compute level.

claims.claim: 300-3,000+ tok/s single-stream depending on model size

independent_sources.finding: Vendor page confirms ASIC architecture with RDU units. No specific throughput benchmarks published.
CRN coverage confirms SN3000 exists and targets LLM inference. No independent performance verification found.

limitations: Pricing not public; sold as complete systems
Throughput claims from stage 02 are vendor-only
Limited ecosystem compared to NVIDIA CUDA
System-level pricing makes per-GPU comparison impossible

summary: Groq LPU is the most verified emerging architecture with independent third-party confirmation of ~1,000 tok/s/user. Cerebras WSE-3 exists but stage 02 benchmark numbers appear inflated (official 750 tok/s vs claimed 1,800-3,000 tok/s). SambaNova SN3000 lacks independent verification — all claims are vendor-only. All three architectures share the key advantage of on-chip SRAM eliminating memory wall, but all lack the flexibility and ecosystem of GPU platforms.
key_finding: Emerging architectures (Groq, Cerebras, SambaNova) excel at single-stream low-latency inference but lack independent verification of their claims. Groq has the strongest independent verification. Cerebras official numbers are lower than stage 02 peak claims. SambaNova has no independent benchmarks. None match GPU flexibility for model switching or multi-stream aggregate throughput.
